title: Fix attack path tests failing due to run target outside engagement scope
goal: Update _create_scoped_engagement (or create a new variant) to include '10.0.1.10' in the scope allowlist when used by the cloud/inferred edge tests. The scope allowlist should include both the named hosts and the IP address: allowlist_json: {'hosts': ['app.example.test', 'api.example.test', '10.0.1.10']}. Alternatively, change the run configuration targets to use 'app.example.test' instead of '10.0.1.10'. The cleanest fix is to add '10.0.1.10' to the scope allowlist in the shared _create_scoped_engagement helper since the first passing test also uses 10.0.1.10 in inventory.
scope: api/tests/test_attack_paths.py has two failing tests: test_attack_path_summary_adds_review_only_inferred_identity_cloud_edges and test_attack_path_summary_retains_unmatched_findings_as_low_confidence. Both fail with KeyError: 'id' when accessing run['id'] after creating a run. The actual cause is the run creation returns HTTP 400 with 'configured target 10.0.1.10 is outside the approved engagement scope'. The engagement scope allows hosts=['app.example.test', 'api.example.test'] but the run configuration uses targets={'hosts': ['10.0.1.10']}. The target IP is not in the scope allowlist, so the run creation is correctly rejected by the scope guard added in backlog-100.

inputs.root_cause: The _create_scoped_engagement helper creates a scope with allowlist {'hosts': ['app.example.test', 'api.example.test']}. The run configuration uses targets {'hosts': ['10.0.1.10']} which does not match the scope. The scope enforcement from backlog-100 rejects this. Tests were written before strict scope enforcement was added.
